purpose: Turn the public source registry into an executable research router. Priority is based on the probability that an archive can close an existing object-text-circulation question, not on collection size or institutional prestige.
priority_rules: Prefer holdings where slides and documentary apparatus coexist.
Prefer a named historical actor, series, cabinet, catalogue, subscription, or transaction over an aggregate collection description.
Prefer archives that can close an already identified corpus event or surviving-object node.
Treat current custody, maker attribution, historical ownership, publication, subscription, donation, transfer and later cataloguing as separate relations.
Do not convert repository aggregate counts into nineteenth-century slide totals.
A contextual route becomes direct only when a slide-specific archival bridge is demonstrated.

tier_1_close_now.target: History of Science Museum, Oxford — RMS Archive + RMS slide cabinet
tier_1_close_now.research_question: Can nineteenth-century RMS donation, exhibition and receipt notices in the corpus be connected to institutional acquisition records and surviving slides?
existing_corpus_bridge: maker names and series already extracted
tier_1_close_now.expected_payoff: Potential text → institutional record → surviving object closure at item or series level.

tier_1_close_now.target: Quekett Microscopical Club archive and slide collection
tier_1_close_now.research_question: Can Cole's Studies in Microscopical Science preparations be reconnected to issue numbers after the Library/Cabinet split?
existing_corpus_bridge: 1883 Quekett report: completed volume in Library
1883 report: accompanying specimens possessed by subscription in Cabinet
Quekett archive label transcriptions and tray photographs
tier_1_close_now.expected_payoff: Direct test of referential binding and institutional re-addressing.

tier_1_close_now.research_question: What did the working ecology of a professional nineteenth-century slide preparer look like from raw specimen through tools, stain, mounting, label and cabinet?
tier_1_close_now.expected_payoff: Workshop-level chain rather than biography; strong material-practice section or standalone case.

tier_1_close_now.target: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn Historical Archives
tier_1_close_now.research_question: Can the 1880 preparation catalogue and the June 1880 RMS twelve-slide shipment be connected to internal preparation-department records, correspondence or accounts?
tier_1_close_now.expected_payoff: Could move Naples from catalogue ↔ exhibition closure to transaction-level circulation history.

tier_1_close_now.target: Museo de La Plata — División Ficología + Archivo Histórico
tier_1_close_now.research_question: Can the surviving Tempère & Peragallo and Möller diatom series be reconnected to their nineteenth-century numbering, acquisition/exchange history and documentary apparatus?
existing_corpus_bridge: Tempère & Peragallo selected as Cole comparator
Museo de La Plata explicitly preserves both named collections
Historical Archive preserves Museum correspondence from 1884 onward
documents_to_seek: Frenguelli annotations or later recataloguing records
tier_1_close_now.expected_payoff: A surviving object + numbered-series + institutional-archive comparator to Cole in one repository; potentially the cleanest way to test a second model of slide publication.

tier_2_build_comparators.target: MNHN Histothèque — Van Tieghem core collection
tier_2_build_comparators.research_question: How did botanical preparations function when the slide itself could remain the only surviving visual documentation of published research?
tier_2_build_comparators.expected_payoff: A different relation between publication and slide: slide as surviving evidential image rather than distributed edition component.

tier_2_build_comparators.target: NHM Vienna — Albert Grunow diatom collection
tier_2_build_comparators.research_question: How did sample numbers coordinate raw material, slides, catalogues, drawings, annotated books and published images?
tier_2_build_comparators.comparison_to: Cole issue number and Croydon cabinet address
tier_2_build_comparators.expected_payoff: Comparative indexing ecology: sample number as cross-media address.

tier_2_build_comparators.target: Harvard Farlow diatom slide series and manuscript catalogues
tier_2_build_comparators.research_question: How did numbered commercial/scientific slide series remain navigable across cards, manuscript catalogues, boxes and physical slides?
tier_2_build_comparators.comparison_to: Cole synchronized serial; Tempère-Peragallo numbered publication series
documents_to_seek: H. L. Smith 1–750 cards and trays
tier_2_build_comparators.expected_payoff: Multiple series in one repository permit controlled comparison of numbering and collection afterlife.

tier_2_build_comparators.target: McGill — Natural History Society of Montreal / Montreal Microscopical Society
tier_2_build_comparators.research_question: How were slide exchange, acquisition, display and cataloguing organized in a North American microscopical society?
tier_2_build_comparators.expected_payoff: A geographically independent society comparator with unusually complete institutional records.

tier_2_build_comparators.research_question: How were petrographic thin sections embedded in experiment records, apparatus, photographs and rock-deformation research?
tier_2_build_comparators.expected_payoff: Instrument/section/experiment chain for petrographic microscopy beyond commercial slide culture.

tier_3_global_extension.target: University of Padua — Giovanni Canestrini arachnological slides
tier_3_global_extension.question: Can maker/contributor labels and type revision recover exchange among Canestrini and other European arachnologists?
Can raw sediment, isolated specimen, type slide, drawing and field note be followed as one evidential transformation chain?

tier_3_global_extension.target: Smithsonian — Conger/Thomas Christian Richmond research files
tier_3_global_extension.question: Which nineteenth-century American slide makers, exchanges and society events can be recovered by reversing Conger's later historical reconstruction back into contemporary sources?

tier_3_global_extension.target: National Museum of Nature and Science, Japan — microalgae herbarium
tier_3_global_extension.question: Which named subcollections preserve historical slide + sketch/photographic-plate/database crosswalks, and do any reach the nineteenth-century Japanese preparation trade found in the bibliography?

tier_3_global_extension.target: Te Papa — Natural History stores + Te Papa Archives
tier_3_global_extension.question: Can Colonial Museum/Hector records be connected to present slide holdings or nineteenth-century microscopy acquisition routes?

tier_3_global_extension.target: Iziko South African Museum — Entomology slides
tier_3_global_extension.question: Which named nineteenth-century subcollections, if any, survive among the aggregate microscope-slide holdings?

tier_3_global_extension.target: UCT — Bolus Herbarium / Harry Bolus Papers
tier_3_global_extension.question: Can botanical correspondence and collecting registers produce a slide/preparation-specific microscopy bridge in late nineteenth-century southern Africa?

recommended_next_actions: Do not broaden the source registry merely for geographic symmetry; add repositories when they expose a recoverable documentary apparatus.
Search the Quekett label transcription/database before requesting new photography; existing metadata and tray photographs may answer the first Cole-survival question cheaply.
Treat Museo de La Plata as the first Tempère & Peragallo object-level comparator because the named series and an institutional archive coexist there.
Use Elcock as the first maker-workshop case because tools, materials, labels, unfinished specimens and finished slides survive together.
Use Grunow/Farlow/MNHN as controlled comparators for different numbering and indexing systems after the Cole article architecture is stable.
For each archive visit or enquiry, request old catalogues/registers and current cabinet/tray crosswalks before requesting broad digitisation.
